content.body:
The Mk.IXc model Spitfire was the RAF's answer to Germany's early Fw190 "A" series Butcherbird fighter. Climb rate, top speed, and ammo load out were all improved markedly over the Mk.Vb, producing a faster, much quicker climbing Spitfire with twice the 20mm cannon rounds to expend in combat compared to its immediate predecessor in the Mk.Vb. The even later E wing variant replaced the 2 x .303 light machine guns in the wings with a .50 caliber heavy machine gun in each wing, increasing its hitting power over even shorter required firing solutions.
When later variants were deployed into theatres of conflict, the IX model still enjoyed more combat success than any other Spitfire variant as its combination of climb, speed, and turn rate had produced almost an ideal configuration, and it was available in large numbers as well. Later variants that followed the IX model were notably faster but suffered in the turning role as a result of increased weight and wing loading extending out beyond what might, arguably ... be called ideal when one considers the still dominant nature of dogfighting in the realms of air to air combat during the typical WWII fighter combat experience.
As the war moved East into Germany the Spitfires weakness was finally exposed, as it lacked the fuel capacity to penetrate deeply enough into German airspace to do combat and return home to Allied bases which were still a long way from the eastern reaches of the German homeland.
content.brief: TYPE: Fighter Interceptor CREW: 1 WEIGHT: 3402 kg MAX SPEED: 657 km/h ARMAMENT: 2 x 20mm Hispano Cannon 4 x .303 cal. LMG
